text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- "A time of progress ..lies ahead of us" said Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic after casting his vote at run off local elections Sunday.
- The Yugoslav federal government bans free import of raw sugar.
- The Yugoslav securities commission approved the issue of shares to the total value of 46.3 million dinars.
- There will be no devaluation of the dinar and rumours to that effect are individual speculations, says Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.
- Yugoslav economy is in dire need of additional working capital to overcome its present insolvency and indebtedness, says economics expert Jovan Rankovic.

- A delegation of the World Bank is arriving in Yugoslavia Monday on a visit considered to be important as a preparation for Yugoslavia joinining the International Monetery Fund and gaining access to facilities extended by the World Bank in financing development programmes, says deputy National Bank governor Bozidar Gazivgoda
- Trial of U.S. dollar forgers opens in Serbia's southern town of Nis, $4.5 million forged notes seized.
NASA BORBA
- The opposition is leading in central Belgrade municipalities and has won most towns in Serbia, according to partial unofficial results of Serbia's local elections.
- Money supply was increased ahead of the November 3 elections in Yugoslavia to reach around five billion dinars, up from 4.5 billion, Nasa Borba learns from federal government sources.

- Croatian government objects to plans of Serbs in U.N. administered Eastern Slavonia to celebrate the anniversary of entry of the former Yugoslav people's army (JNA) in that town in 1991 describing it as a threat to peaceful reintegration of the area into Croatia.
- The entire territory of Montenegro became an off-shore centre on November 16 which will have a 2.5 percent profit tax, lower than in Cyprus.
- McDonald's plans to have 60 restaurants in Yugoslavia by the turn of the century, says marketing manager for Yugoslavia Vesna Milosevic.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- The newly-elected Montenegrin parliament holds its constituent session in Cetinje Monday.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Yugoslav and Macedonian Red cross sign cooperation agreement in Belgrade on Sunday.
- Aleksinac coal mine, closed since 1989, plans to start exploitation of a new shaft estimated to have six million tonnes of coal deposits.
BORBA

- Zastava cars has exported to the vaue of 10.2 million German marks in the first nine months of 1996 and plans to reach exports of 20 million German marks by end of year, says director Miodrag Bogdanovic.
-- Belgrade Newsroom, 381 11 222 4254
